text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) says it sees no reason to implement any special measures to react to the decline of the Czech crown.
- Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said the unsuccessful refendums on NATO membership and direct presidential elections last weekend would not have a negative impact on Slovakia's economy.

- Opposition parties have welcomed the resignation of Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik, saying his move only showed that Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar was unable to create conditions for pursuing the state's foreign interests in the longer term.
- Alexander Rezes, Chairman of the Board of major steel producer VSZ, said he was convinced that Slovakia would produce cars with the main focus on exports to the former Soviet Union.
- VSZ director Jan Smerek said VSZ was negotiating with several Japanese car producers represented by banking house Nomura.
SME - Meciar's ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) said Hamzik's resignation was his personal and private decision.
- President Michal Kovac has yet to officially accept Hamzik's resignation. Kovac said he was waiting for the government's proposal of Hamzik's successor.

- European Union Foreign and Security Policy Comissioner Hans van den Broek will visit Bratislava on Thursday, where he is expected to voice the EU's opinion on the development of democratic principles in Slovakia.

- Herbert Boesch, a co-chairman of the EU-Slovak joint parliamentary committee, said the recent failure to carry out a legal referendum on NATO membership and presidential elections could have a negative influence on the EU report on Slovakia's preparedness for EU membership.

- The ultra-right Slovak National Party (SNS), a junior member of the ruling coalition, said it would initiate coalition talks on reconsidering Slovak foreign policy to push it towards military neutrality.

PRAVDA - The state-owned gas distributor SPP said it would have to increase retail prices by some 30 to 35 percent to make a profit from distribution to small private customers. But the company said it did not plan any price hikes within the next two years.
- The Slovak government is expected to discuss energy price increase next June.

- Slovakia's largest drug producer Slovakofarma posted a net consolidated profit of 554 million crowns, calculated according to international accounting standards, which is a year-on-year incease of about 15 percent.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Engineering company Detva said it planned to enter the U.S and South American markets through a network of local trade partners.
